gen-gf-bruno-ace-general-sans: Reading here feels smooth, with lowercase that fills the line and curves that never snag. General Sans carries that ease beside Bruno Ace, whose ruler-drawn, open-mouthed letters give the pair its edge.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-orbit: Open-ended curves, letters floating apart, nothing crowded. Bruno Ace, with its ruler-drawn line, earns its keep big and short, while Orbit sits beneath with rope-like strokes that stay uniform.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-science-gothic: Bruno Ace draws every line with a ruler's constancy, its counters staying open to the outside. And Science Gothic, with stroke ends set far apart, reads one letter at a time beneath it.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-manrope: Ruler-drawn and unhurried, Bruno Ace lingers over each character while Manrope opens a bright gap at every curve. The heading makes the statement; the body quietly keeps text moving.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-montserrat: Bruno Ace holds its ruler-drawn line steady while its counters stay open to the outside, one character per beat. It earns its keep big and short, with sans-serif Montserrat behind it.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-satoshi: Bruno Ace lingers on every character, its ruler-drawn line and open counters giving headings real presence. Satoshi, with a soaring x-height, can sit comfortably a size or two below the heading.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-switzer: Bruno Ace lingers, one ruler-drawn character per beat, counters open to the outside. Switzer, tubular and wire-like with a tall waist line, stays crisp and approachable paragraph after paragraph.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-work-sans: Distinctive from the first letter, Bruno Ace draws a ruler-drawn line around counters that stay open. Work Sans does the quieter job, a contemporary sans-serif with a high mean line that holds up in running text.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-sc-archivo: Archivo reads like an editorial plain sans, its curves opening outward under a commanding x-height. But Bruno Ace SC, with its steady line and spread-out letters, loses its beaded rhythm if made small.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-sc-fs-asap: Asap reads clearly, its sans-serif c forms open arcs and its lowercase nearly matching the capitals. And Bruno Ace SC, its letters strung like beads on a long thread, supplies the contrast.
